Summarise an FMEA Pareto Analysis

Source: R/fmea.R
fmea_pareto_summary.Rd

Reads the headline figures out of a Pareto analysis produced by r4subrisk::risk_pareto() so they can drive the dashboard's FMEA summary boxes. This is a pure, non-reactive helper.

Usage

fmea_pareto_summary(pareto)

Arguments

pareto

A risk_pareto object, as returned by r4subrisk::risk_pareto(). Expected to carry the columns rpn and vital_few and the attributes total_rpn, n_vital_few, and cum_cutoff.

Value

A named list with elements:

n_risks

Number of risks in the register (nrow(pareto)).

total_rpn

Total RPN across the register.

n_vital_few

Number of "vital few" risks that make up the cumulative share cut-off.

cum_cutoff

The cumulative-share cut-off used (for example 0.8).

top_rpn

The largest single RPN in the register (0 if empty).

vital_few_share

Fraction of all risks that are "vital few" (0 if empty).

Details

Every value it returns is read straight from the Pareto object (its rows and its total_rpn, n_vital_few, and cum_cutoff attributes); the helper computes no new risk scores. It is therefore easy to unit test on its own.

Examples

if (requireNamespace("r4subrisk", quietly = TRUE)) {
  ev <- suppressMessages(generate_demo_evidence(40, seed = 1))
  risks <- suppressMessages(r4subrisk::evidence_to_risks(ev))
  reg <- suppressMessages(r4subrisk::create_risk_register(risks))
  fmea_pareto_summary(r4subrisk::risk_pareto(reg))
}
#> $n_risks
#> [1] 11
#> 
#> $total_rpn
#> [1] 291
#> 
#> $n_vital_few
#> [1] 6
#> 
#> $cum_cutoff
#> [1] 0.8
#> 
#> $top_rpn
#> [1] 75
#> 
#> $vital_few_share
#> [1] 0.5454545
#>
